name: Rephaiah
overview: Rephaiah was a male member of the tribe of Issachar, known specifically as the son of Tola. His identity is primarily grounded in this familial connection, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:2. There are no additional notes or distinguishing details about his life or role beyond this lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Rephaiah means "y-h-v-h heals," reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's healing power. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful declaration of divine healing as part of its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Rephaiah was the son of Tola, establishing his place within the family line of Issachar. Beyond this father-son relationship, no further family connections or descendants are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Rephaiah's significance in the biblical narrative lies chiefly in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Issachar, as a descendant of Tola. While the biblical text does not elaborate on his personal deeds or contributions, his mention preserves the lineage important for understanding the tribal structures and heritage of Israel. His name's meaning also subtly points to the faithfulness of God as a healer, which aligns with the broader biblical testimony of God's care for His people.
